"'''Baby, I Love Your Way/Freebird Medley (Free Baby)'''" is a song by American [[dance-pop]] band [[Will to Power (band)|Will to Power]]. The song combines elements of two previously recorded [[rock music|rock]] songs: "[[Baby, I Love Your Way]]", a number-12 [[Billboard Hot 100|''Billboard'' Hot 100]] hit from 1976 by English musician [[Peter Frampton]],<ref>{{cite magazine|url=https://www.billboard.com/music/peter-frampton/chart-history|title=Peter Frampton Chart History (Hot 100)|magazine=[[Billboard (magazine)|Billboard]]|access-date=August 29, 2020}}</ref> and "[[Free Bird]]" by American [[Southern rock]] band [[Lynyrd Skynyrd]], which reached number 19 on the Hot 100 chart in 1975.<ref>{{cite magazine|url=https://www.billboard.com/music/lynyrd-skynyrd/chart-history|title=Lynyrd Skynyrd Chart History (Hot 100)|magazine=Billboard|access-date=August 29, 2020}}</ref> Suzi Carr is the female vocalist and a producer for the song.<ref name="aus"/>

In the United States, the medley spent one week at number one on the ''Billboard'' Hot 100 and also peaked at number two on the ''Billboard'' [[Hot Adult Contemporary Tracks|Adult Contemporary]] chart. Internationally, the song topped the Canadian, Norwegian, and Portuguese charts and reached the top 20 in Australia, Ireland, New Zealand, the United Kingdom, and West Germany. In March and April 2009, [[VH1]] ran a countdown of the "100 Greatest One Hit Wonders of the 80s", placing it at number 97 despite the group having another US top-10 hit in 1991 with a [[cover version]] of the 1975 [[10cc]] hit "[[I'm Not in Love]]".<ref name="hot100"/>

"Baby, I Love Your Way/Freebird Medley (Free Baby)" is a song by American dance-pop band Will to Power. The song combines elements of two previously recorded rock songs: "Baby, I Love Your Way", a number-12 Billboard Hot 100 hit from 1976 by English musician Peter Frampton, and "Free Bird" by American Southern rock band Lynyrd Skynyrd, which reached number 19 on the Hot 100 chart in 1975. Suzi Carr is the female vocalist and a producer for the song.

In the United States, the medley spent one week at number one on the Billboard Hot 100 and also peaked at number two on the Billboard Adult Contemporary chart. Internationally, the song topped the Canadian, Norwegian, and Portuguese charts and reached the top 20 in Australia, Ireland, New Zealand, the United Kingdom, and West Germany. In March and April 2009, VH1 ran a countdown of the "100 Greatest One Hit Wonders of the 80s", placing it at number 97 despite the group having another US top-10 hit in 1991 with a cover version of the 1975 10cc hit "I'm Not in Love".
